practical_derivations.interpretation: The slope is the period: elapsed time divided by number of full oscillations, 1.6 s.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The slope is temperature rise per second, 0.08 °C/s. For 0.100 kg of water with c = 4200 J/(kg K), the water gains energy at mc(dT/dt) = 33.6 W. A roughly 35 W heater allows about 1.4 W for losses in this idealised example; voltage alone does not set its power.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The slope is speed, 3 cm/s. The 5 cm position intercept does not change speed.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The slope is period, 1.4 s; use the same timing procedure at other lengths to test length dependence.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The speed-time gradient is acceleration, 0.20 m/s².
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The slope is extension per force, 12 mm/N. Stiffness is its reciprocal: 1/0.012 = about 83 N/m.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The mass-versus-volume gradient is density, 0.80 g/cm³ = 800 kg/m³. Total container-plus-liquid mass would instead have a container-mass intercept.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The plotted relation is 1/F = d/M. Gradient = 1/M = 0.50 N⁻¹ m⁻¹, so the fixed moment M = 2.0 N m.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The slope is temperature rise per minute, 0.8 °C/min over this short interval; it is not collector efficiency.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The energy-time gradient is useful lifting power, 3 W; the electrical or human input power can be greater.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The pressure-depth gradient equals ρg, 10 000 Pa/m; dividing by g = 10 N/kg gives ρ = 1000 kg/m³.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The slope is liquid-column length change per temperature degree for this apparatus, 0.6 mm/°C. It is not a volume-expansion coefficient.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The calibration slope is sensitivity, 0.7 mm/°C. The fitted line has a length offset; it need not pass through zero.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: For energy vertically against temperature rise, the slope is heat capacity C = mc = 800 J/K. With mass 0.20 kg, c = C/m = 4000 J/(kg K).
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The black-can slope is (70 − 78)/(100 − 0) = −0.08 °C/s. The shiny-can slope is (73 − 78)/(100 − 0) = −0.05 °C/s. The black can has the steeper negative gradient and cools faster under the matched conditions.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The wavelength-period slope is wave speed: 20 cm/s = 0.20 m/s because λ = cT and T = 1/f.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The angle ratio has no unit: the fitted slope is 1. Both axes use the same angle measure, and r = i.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The sine quantities and their ratio have no unit. The slope is refractive index 1.5 for sin i vertically against sin r.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The one-way reflector distance versus round-trip time slope is c/2 = 170 m/s. Therefore sound speed c = 340 m/s.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The slope is open-circuit voltage per series-aiding cell, 1.45 V per cell. Cell count has no physical unit.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: With potential difference vertically against current, the slope is resistance, 12 Ω, at approximately fixed temperature.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The energy-time slope is electrical input power, 5 W. For comparison, a steady 5 V and 1 A input would give VI = 5 W.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The slope is the measured change in pull per current over this limited illustrative range, 2 N/A. The 0.1 N intercept can include a force-gauge zero offset; it is not a universal force law.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)

practical_derivations.interpretation: The slope is secondary voltage per turn, 0.05 V per turn, equal to Vp/Np in the ideal model. These open-circuit readings do not measure efficiency.
practical_derivations.rubric_allocation: 5 graph + 3 gradient + 8 plan (1 arrangement + 3 measurement + 2 control/precaution + 1 table + 1 conclusion)
